analysis.title: Heineken N.V. Model update
key_insights: RBC raises its adjusted present value (APV) price target on Heineken to €87 from €84 and maintains Sector Perform, following the 3Q26 results.
RBC forecasts 2026E organic EBIT growth of 5.6%, then 3.1% in 2027E and 3.0% in 2028E. It assumes flattish margins consistent with low-mid single digit organic EBIT growth.
New CEO Rafa Oliveira will detail his plans with the full year results on 10 February 2027. RBC expects more visibility on long-term trajectory in 1H 2027.
2026E group organic revenue growth is 2.6% (volume +1.7%, price +0.9%). Asia Pacific is the strongest region at +11.0% organic, with volume +9.0%.
Americas organic revenue is forecast flat in 2026E (volume -1.0%, price +1.0%). Europe is +0.8%, and Africa & the Middle East +5.0%.

Revenue estimates rise to €31.0bn (2026E), €32.3bn (2027E) and €33.2bn (2028E) from €30.9bn, €32.2bn and €33.1bn. EPS (operations, diluted) rises to €5.09, €5.48 and €5.66 from €5.08, €5.46 and €5.63.

The APV gives €82 per share (equity value €37.8bn plus €6.8bn tax shield). Discounting forward 12 months at an 8.0% cost of equity, net of the forecast dividend, gives the €87 target. Terminal growth is 2.5%.

Upside scenario is €132 (revenue growth +150bps and EBIT margin +250bps vs base, FY28-40E). Downside scenario is €50 (same magnitudes below base). Implied total returns are +75% and -32% against the €76.78 price.
The positive case is improved expectations management, steady capital allocation and increased marketing investment after a decade of decline. RBC says this supports share gains and category growth.
The negative case is near-term macro headwinds and intense competition in Asia, which make the mid-term growth ambition look distant.
At €87 the target implies about 16% total return from €76.78. The stock trades at 15.1x 2026E P/E and 14.0x 2027E, with a 2.7% dividend yield.

Valuation table: Heineken is on 15.3x 2026E P/E and 8.3x EV/EBITDA, against a beverages average of 16.1x P/E and 10.9x EV/EBITDA. Anheuser-Busch InBev is Outperform with a €95 target, and Carlsberg is Outperform with a DKK 1,050 target.

market_movers.rationale: Target raised to €87 from €84 after 3Q26 results and a model update. Rating unchanged, with solid growth offset by Asia competition and macro headwinds.
Listed in the peer valuation table as Outperform with a €95 target (previous €73 price column shows €73).
Carlsberg is listed in the peer valuation table as Outperform, 2026E P/E 14.3x.
Diageo is listed in the peer valuation table as Outperform, 2026E P/E 16.2x.
BAT is listed in the peer valuation table as Underperform, 2026E P/E 13.6x.
Beiersdorf is listed in the peer valuation table as Underperform, 2026E P/E 21.0x.

sector_views.rationale: Heineken is Sector Perform, and the group's brewers range from Outperform (AB InBev, Carlsberg, Diageo) to Sector Perform (Heineken, Pernod Ricard, Campari).

earnings_insights: Heineken 3Q26 results were published before this model update, and RBC raised its forecasts afterward. The report gives no 3Q figures.
RBC 2026E EPS (operations, diluted) is €5.09 vs previous €5.08, 2027E €5.48 vs €5.46, and 2028E €5.66 vs €5.63. These are RBC estimates, not reported figures.
RBC 2026E EBITA (after restructuring) is €4.72bn, 2027E €5.00bn and 2028E €5.16bn. 2025A EBITA was €4.28bn.
RBC 2026E DPS is €2.10 and 2027E €2.23, against 2025A of €1.90.
Full year results will be published on 10 February 2027, with the new CEO's plans.
risk_factors: Worsened macro trends in Vietnam and Nigeria.
Weaker consumer sentiment and tighter inventory management by retailers in Europe.
Deteriorating organic sales momentum even with higher marketing investment.
Lower alcohol consumption, particularly by Gen Z, as a long-term risk.
Outperformance of mass brands could create negative price/mix, though it could revive volume growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Improved expectations management, steady capital allocation and higher marketing spend should support share gains and category growth, giving confidence in delivering on growth expectations.
tension_points.bear_case: Near-term macro headwinds and intense competition in Asia are likely to weigh on top-line growth, making the mid-term growth ambition seem distant.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Deteriorating organic sales momentum even with further increases in marketing investment would be a downside risk, as would worsened macro trends in Vietnam or Nigeria.

theme_stances.key_argument: Long overdue increased marketing investment after a decade of decline should support share gains and category growth.
theme_stances.evidence: long overdue increased investment in marketing
